desc: Ideation/proof: collapse floor dimension; per-path bottleneck m gives cost max(|Y-Z|, Y+Z-2*m); grid widest-path value M preserved by maximum spanning tree; answer via LCA min-edge on MaxST.

Implement the complete Python solution: fast integer input parsing; flatten F to id=i*W+j; build right/down edges with weight min(F_u,F_v) packed as sortable integers; Kruskal descending with DSU to build the maximum spanning tree; compact adjacency; iterative rooting; binary-lifting tables (up and min-edge-to-ancestor); answer each query as abs(Y-Z) if same cell else max(abs(Y-Z), Y+Z-2*M) with M=path minimum edge.

Validate edge cases: H=1 or W=1, equal heights, same block different floors, M<min(Y,Z), M between Y and Z, M>=max(Y,Z), path forced through height 1; cross-check random small grids against brute-force Dijkstra over (cell, floor) states; confirm sample outputs.

Check memory/performance: N<=250k, E<=500k, Q<=200k; max-size stress audit done — C-level parsing, packed edges, array('i') tables, pre-zipped lifting loops; estimated runtime ~5-8s and peak memory ~130-150MB, within limits.
